name: Learn several songs using four guitar chords
blurb: G, C, D and Em — or with a capo, any key you like — unlock a startling proportion of popular music. The barrier is not the chords, it is the changes and the sore fingertips.
gear: An acoustic guitar with low action
Light-gauge strings while your fingers toughen up
steps: Learn G, C, D and Em one at a time, checking every string rings clean before moving on.
Drill one-minute change exercises between each pair of chords.
Learn a simple down-strum on every beat first, and only then add the up-strokes.
Learn to use a capo so you can play in any key with the same four shapes.
Learn three songs completely, including intros and endings.
Add Am and a simplified F, which together with the first four cover most of the rest.
tips: Fingertip pain lasts about two weeks and then stops for good. Short daily sessions build calluses faster than long ones.
Press just behind the fret, not on top of it, and arch your fingers so they clear the neighbouring strings.
Keep strumming through the changes even if the chord is late. Rhythm matters more than accuracy to a listener.
proof: You play three songs all the way through, in time, without stopping at a chord change.
